subject: Final MAP alignment & go/no-go window (SOW + start date)
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Holt <sabrina.holt@cloudlineretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft and proposed evaluation cadence

Sabrina —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call I attached the mutual action plan (v3) that folds in the evaluation milestones, required evidence for the security/compliance review, and the proposed trial/start window. Highlights: 

- Evaluation phase: 2 weeks (functional + perf) with predefined prompt set and latency targets.
- Security evidence: we will provide SOC2 excerpt + trace/sample logs by EOW.
- Signoff window: requested signature by 2026-07-05 to enable a 2026-07-19 production start.

Can you confirm procurement timing on your side and whether the requested signature window (by 7/5) is achievable? If procurement needs a different cadence, tell me the latest date that still supports your internal launch target.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_v3.xlsx (MAP), draft checklist for evaluation.

Thanks,
Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: mutual_action_plan_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Sabrina Holt <sabrina.holt@cloudlineretail.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@cloudlineretail.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft and proposed evaluation cadence

Lukas —

Appreciate the high level and the MAP. Quick notes from procurement and product:

- Procurement: we can review the SOW but need the PO + legal redlines by Friday 7/2 latest to get finance signoff in time. Procurement will likely issue a PO rather than fully executing a countersigned SOW first.
- Product: the 2-week eval is fine but we may push cutover to the third week if we encounter minor perf regressions. Preferred production start date is the week of 7/19.

I attached a PO draft for your T&E — it's not final but gives our finance team what they need to block budget. If you can accept PO-first, we can run parallel legal review.

Sabrina
Sabrina Holt
Head of Integrations | Cloudline Retail
[attachment: cloudline_po_draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP draft and proposed evaluation cadence

Looping legal and ops context: we should accept the PO-first approach (common for larger retailers) but ensure we have a matching SOW + signature path that covers SLAs and data residency commitments before the cutover. Action items:

- Lukas: confirm we can take a PO as a commitment to begin the evaluation spike (yes/no).
- Karthik: please flag any contract terms that require escalated approval (pricing overrides, SLA exceptions).
- Marissa: keep customer success in the loop for onboarding the pilot users.

I want to avoid needing a formal SLA exception later. If a request comes in, escalate to Markus for signoff.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP draft and proposed evaluation cadence

Quick review from pricing & legal:

- Pricing: recommended to honor the quoted unit rates in the MAP for the evaluation period. No one-off credits required.
- Legal: the PO-first approach is acceptable but we need a countersigned SOW before the production cutover. There is one clause (data retention) where Cloudline's ask pushes beyond our standard terms — if that remains, we'll require an SLA exception.

If that exception is needed, we will route to Markus Klein for approval. I attached a short SLA-exception-request doc to use if Cloudline pushes the retention term.

-Karthik
[attachment: sla-exception-request.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Holt <sabrina.holt@cloudlineretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Final SOW attached — target signature window and go/no-go

Sabrina —

Thanks for the PO draft and the timeline guidance. We've taken the MAP to final and attached the SOW for countersignature. Key points and next steps: 

- We can accept the PO as a trigger to start the evaluation spike, provided Cloudline acknowledges the evaluation acceptance criteria in the MAP.
- Please aim to return either (A) a countersigned SOW by 2026-07-05, or (B) an executed PO plus confirmation of acceptance criteria by 2026-07-02. Either path keeps the production start target of 2026-07-19.
- If Cloudline requests stretched data retention beyond our standard terms we will need an SLA exception; Karthik has prepared the request form and will route to Markus for approval.

If you confirm the preferred path (SOW vs PO-first), we'll kick off a brief legal alignment call tomorrow to finish outstanding redlines. 

Final SOW attached: redwood_sow_final.pdf. DocuSign link below for convenience.

Best,
Lukas
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
